candidates.label: isBasedOn
candidates.comment: A derivation relation between a creative work and the resource (another work, product, or URL) from which it is adapted or modified. candidates.label: byArtist

candidates.label: editor

candidates.label: creator

candidates.label: composer
candidates.comment: A creative role relation between an event or music composition and the organization or person who wrote it. Also called "writer", "creator", "author of music". candidates.label: founder
candidates.comment: A founder relation between an organization and the person or organization that established it. Also called: established by, created by, initiated by. candidates.label: creditedTo

Examples: "Album 'Red and Blue'" credited to "Stefani Germanotta Band", "Single 'X'" credited to "The Session Musicians", "Soundtrack" credited to "Various Artists".

candidates.label: sponsor

candidates.label: publishedBy

candidates.label: isStoreOn
candidates.comment: A platform hosting relation between an online store and the e-commerce marketplace where it operates. Also called hosted on, operates on, platform for, marketplace for. candidates.label: tickerSymbol

candidates.label: currenciesAccepted

candidates.label: merchant
candidates.comment: A seller relation between an order and the organization or person acting as the seller. Also called: seller, vendor, retailer. Examples: "Online Order merchant Amazon", "Local Purchase merchant Boutique Store", "Service Booking merchant Freelancer".

candidates.label: priceSpecification

candidates.label: seller
candidates.comment: The organization or person that offers, sells, leases, lends, or loans goods or services. Also called vendor, merchant, provider, retailer. candidates.label: priceCurrency
candidates.comment: A financial attribute indicating the currency in which a price or price component is expressed. Also called currency type, monetary unit, unit of exchange. candidates.label: price
candidates.comment: A financial attribute indicating the monetary value of an offer, product, or price component. Also called cost, rate, charge, amount. Examples: An offer has a price of '19.99'. chosen_property.label: item

candidates.label: hasRepresentation

candidates.label: representativeOfPage

candidates.label: photo

candidates.label: regionDrained

Examples: "The femoral vein drains region 'the leg'.", "A lymphatic vessel drains region 'the arm'.", "The hepatic portal vein drains region 'the digestive tract'."

candidates.label: naturalProgression
candidates.comment: The expected progression of a medical condition if left untreated. Also called untreated course, disease progression, natural history of condition. Examples: "Common Cold naturalProgression 'resolves in 7-10 days'", "Untreated Diabetes naturalProgression 'leads to complications like neuropathy and kidney failure'", "Flu naturalProgression 'fever and body aches for 3-5 days, then recovery'". Distinct from prognosis, which is a forecast of the likely course of a disease.

candidates.label: comprisedOf
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an anatomical system and the anatomical structures or other systems that physically comprise it. Also called "composed of", "consists of", "includes". Examples: "Circulatory system comprisedOf Heart", "Digestive system comprisedOf Stomach".

candidates.label: unsaturatedFatContent
candidates.comment: An unsaturated fat content relation between nutrition information and the amount of unsaturated fat in grams. Also called grams of unsaturated fat, unsaturated fatty acid amount. Examples: "NutritionInformation unsaturatedFatContent '5 g'", "NutritionInformation unsaturatedFatContent '10.2 g'", "NutritionInformation unsaturatedFatContent '3 g'".

candidates.label: sourcedFrom
candidates.comment: An anatomical origin relation between a nerve and the brain structure from which its neurons originate. Also called "originates from", "nerve pathway source", "derived from brain structure". Examples: "The optic nerve is sourcedFrom the diencephalon", "Cranial nerve V is sourcedFrom the brainstem", "This nerve's neurons are sourcedFrom the spinal cord."

candidates.label: expressedIn
candidates.comment: An expressed in relation between a gene and the anatomical structure, system, or biological entity where its activity has been experimentally observed. Also called: gene activity location, observed in, found in. Examples: "Gene A" expressed in "Brain", "Gene B" expressed in "Liver", "Gene C" expressed in "Digestive System".

candidates.label: isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess
candidates.comment: A biological function relation between a biochemical entity and the biological process it participates in. Also called participates in process, role in biological process, contributes to process. Examples: A protein is isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess 'cell division'. An enzyme is isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess 'metabolism'. A hormone is isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess 'growth regulation'.

candidates.label: primaryPrevention
candidates.comment: A medical attribute indicating a preventative therapy used to avert the initial occurrence of a medical condition. Also called preventative measure, initial prevention, prophylactic therapy. Examples: A medical condition has a primary prevention of 'vaccination'. Heart disease has a primary prevention of 'healthy diet'. Infection has a primary prevention of 'hand washing'.

candidates.label: containedIn
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: containsPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and another smaller place that it contains. Also called "includes place", "encompasses", "holds". Examples: "Country 'France' containsPlace 'Paris'", "City 'Paris' containsPlace 'Eiffel Tower'". Distinct from containedIn or containedInPlace, which are the inverse relations.

candidates.label: containsSeason
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a radio, TV, or video game series and a creative work season that is part of it. Also called "includes season", "has season", "season of series". Examples: "TV series 'Friends' containsSeason 'Season 1'", "Video game series 'Halo' containsSeason 'Halo: Combat Evolved'".

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: hasDefinedTerm
candidates.comment: A term inclusion relation between a defined term set or taxon and one of its contained defined terms. Also called contains term, includes term, term within. Examples: "A medical glossary has a defined term for 'hypertension'.", "A taxonomy has a defined term for 'Homo sapiens'.", "The dictionary has a defined term for 'algorithm'."

candidates.label: includesObject
candidates.comment: A composition relation between an offer or product collection and the specific products and their quantities it contains. Also called composed of, contains, comprises, consists of, has as object. Examples: An offer includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 2 apples. A product collection includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 5 books. A demand includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 1 car.

candidates.label: hasCategoryCode
candidates.comment: A code inclusion relation between a category code set and one of its contained category codes. Also called contains code, includes code, code within. Examples: "A product category set has a category code for electronics.", "A medical code set has a category code for diseases.", "The classification system has a category code for services."

candidates.label: includesAttraction
candidates.comment: An attraction inclusion relation between a tourist destination and a tourist attraction located within it. Also called contains attraction, destination attraction, features attraction. Examples: "A tourist destination includes an attraction like a museum.", "The city includes an attraction for historical sites.", "This destination features a famous includes attraction."

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: includedComposition
candidates.comment: A composition inclusion relation between a music composition and a smaller music composition that is part of it. Also called part of composition, contains composition, movement of. Examples: "A symphony has an included composition as a movement.", "A musical work includes a composition.", "This composition contains several included compositions.". Distinct from hasPart, which is a general part-whole relation for creative works.
